title: Mark the evidence where it sits
statement: In guided practice, mark the key quote in place in the text rather than lifting it out, since extracting it does the locating step for the learner, out of sight.
detail: As built, a Grade 9 prototype lifted the key quote out of the script and set it full-width in guided practice. Its review made keeping the script on the left with the quote marked in place a priority item, with the unpicking on the right. Its reason is that marking in place shows where the evidence came from, and locating evidence in the text is the skill being taught, while extracting the quote performs that step invisibly and leaves only the analysis.

evidence.quote: Keep the script on the left in guided practice. Mark the key quote in place within it.
Do not lift the quote out of the script. Extracting it performs the locating step for the child.

Marking it in place shows where the evidence came from — and locating evidence in the text is the SEARCH and FIND skill. Extracting the quote performs that step invisibly and leaves the child only the analysis.
